title: Half-step Gatekeeper Priming Journal
content:
Context:
This is a personal scratchpad for the "half-step gatekeeper" idea — an intermediate, lightweight gating layer between full canary and blunt traffic splits. Intended to be used for small-batch flips where latency and subtle quality regressions are the primary risk, and cost/throughput are secondary.

Goals (quick):
- Give a low-friction route to expose a tiny fraction of production traffic to a new model slice while preserving fast rollback.
- Keep per-token unit cost bounded via micro-batching and short-lived cache priming.
- Provide signal-rich telemetry (latency tail, user-visible errors, semantic regression markers) within 30–90m.

Core idea (1-line):
Introduce a short-duration "half-step" cohort (0.1%–0.5%) routed through a gatekeeper proxy that applies soft-throttles, micro-batches, and an active sentinel that can drop or pin requests based on dynamic heuristics.

Mechanics / playbook notes:
- Cohort size: start 0.1% (per-region), escalate only if all checks green for 40m windows.
- Gatekeeper behavior: accept request -> warm KV cache on prefix heuristics -> allow micro-batch (<=4 concurrent requests) -> apply sampling-based quality checks (semantic similarity probe + rerank check) -> forward to target model.
- Warmup priming: use 25 synthetic prefixes derived from recent customer queries (sampled from last 24h) to pre-populate KV cache on the inference pool before cohort goes live. Keep a short TTL (5m).
- Pinning: allow pin to version X for the cohort by assigning sticky cookie keyed to tenant id (if known) or client-ip hash; pin lifetime 24h default.

Telemetry signals to watch (min set):
- Latency P95 and P99 compared to baseline model (absolute + delta). Thresholds: P99 delta > +120ms -> escalate.
- Token rejection / model error rates (runtime exceptions, OOMs).
- Semantic drift measure: ratio of fallback/low-confidence responses flagged by reranker (threshold > 3x baseline).
- User-visible divergence: fraction of responses with changed intent detection (use small eval suite against live responses).
- Cost delta per 1k tokens (alert if > 1.5x budgeted estimate).

Decision rules (automation + manual):
- Auto-rollback triggers (immediate): any 5m window with runtime exceptions > 0.5% OR P99 delta > +300ms OR OOM spikes.
- Soft-alert triggers (ops pager + Slack): sustained P99 delta > +120ms for 30m OR semantic drift ratio > 2x for 30m.
- Escalation path: engineer on-call -> serving runtime lead -> product owner. If pager not acknowledged in 10m, gatekeeper auto-lifts cohort to 0 traffic (hard-off).

Rollback / escape hatches:
- Fast drop: gatekeeper returns 100% to baseline model within 30s by flipping route table.
- Pinback: immediately pin affected tenants to previous model for 24h (via sticky cookie override).
- Drain-only mode: stop warmup and only accept in-flight requests; do not establish new micro-batches. Useful when errors are creeping but no single catastrophic signal.

Operational checklist (pre-launch):
- [ ] Synthetic priming set curated and stored (25 prefixes). Ticket: INF-4321.
- [ ] Gatekeeper proxy deployed to canary pool with feature flag.
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards: latency deltas, drift ratio, error counts, per-tenant heatmap.
- [ ] Pager set up and escalation documented in runbook.
- [ ] Slack channel #half-step-rollouts pre-notified with quiet window and run owners.
- [ ] Smoke test run with internal clients (2 engineers) for 15m.

Post-launch observation plan (first 3 hours):
- 00–15m: ensure priming completed, confirm micro-batch sizes stable, watch sample traces for anomalies.
- 15–60m: verify P95/P99 within soft thresholds, compare reranker outputs on evaluation prompts every 10m.
- 60–180m: evaluate user-visible metrics and cohort-specific logs; escalate if soft alerts persist 30m.

Open questions / TODOs (brain dump):
- How to best pick the 25 prefixes with minimal PII risk? (anonymize + token filter).
- Should gatekeeper apply a cheap heuristic classifier to drop obviously unsafe requests before hitting the model? Trade-off: false positives vs wasted tokens.
- Consider adding a rolling baseline consumer that replays a tiny sample of cohort traffic through the previous model for A/B quality scoring. Costy but high signal.
- Explore using ephemeral quantization-level change (e.g., lower-bit variant) within gatekeeper to hedge cost spikes. Need SRE buy-in.

Notes to self (quick logs):
- 2025-11-04: sketched proxy flow with Ravi; prototype uses sampling hook in SDK.
- 2025-11-12: ran micro-sim with 10k synthetic requests, saw P99 +90ms when batch size > 6. Cap batch at 4.
- 2025-12-01: Maya suggested reranker threshold tuning; added semantic drift metric.

Useful references and bookmarks:
- Confluence draft: Half-step Gatekeeper (linked above).
- Infra PR: github.com/redwood/release-playbooks/pull/214 (gatekeeper proxy config).
- Telemetry: dashboard ID 'rollout-halfstep-v1' (add to linked_artifacts).

If I pick a name for the feature in prod it should be short — current candidate: "half-step" or "gatekeeper cohort". Prefer "half-step" for notes and logs to reduce noise.

If I forget tomorrow: start at 0.1%, priming 25 prefixes, 4-request micro-batch cap, auto-off on major errors, escalate on sustained P99 drift.

End of scratchpad.
